speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a skin condition on your left dorsal hand; can you tell me how long you've had it and if it is itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis (solar keratosis).

Given your history of frequent sunbathing and outdoor activities, the lesion on your dorsal hand is likely caused by cumulative UV exposure. I want to confirm if the spot feels rough or sandpaper-like to the touch and if you have noticed any changes in its size or color recently.
